**Surah al-Talaq** (Madaniyyah, meaning revealed in Madinah), and its verses are twelve.

﴿O Prophet﴾: the intended meaning is his community, by the indication of what follows; or, say to them. ﴿When you divorce women﴾, i.e., when you intend divorce, ﴿then divorce them for their ʿiddah﴾ (the waiting period), meaning at its beginning, by divorcing them during a state of purity (ṭuhr) in which they have not been touched. This is because the Prophet (ﷺ) explained it that way, as narrated by al-Shaykhan (the two Shaykhs, i.e., al-Bukhari and Muslim). ﴿And count the ʿiddah﴾: preserve it, so that you may take them back before it ends. ﴿And fear Allah, your Lord﴾: obey Him in His commands and prohibitions. ﴿Do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they leave﴾ from them until their ʿiddah ends, ﴿except if they commit a clear immorality﴾, meaning adultery, ﴿mubayyinah﴾, read with a fatḥah and with a kasrah on the yāʾ: bayyanat, or bayyinah, in which case they may go out to have the ḥadd (the prescribed punishment) enforced upon them. ﴿These are the limits of Allah. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that﴾, i.e., after the divorce, ﴿some matter﴾, namely reconciliation, in case it was a single or a double divorce.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 65, verse 2:

﴿Then when they have reached their term﴾ meaning, they have come close to the end of their waiting period (ʿiddah). ﴿then retain them﴾ by taking them back (murājaʿah), ﴿in kindness﴾ without harm. ﴿Or part from them in kindness﴾ leave them until their waiting period ends, and do not harm them by taking them back. ﴿And call to witness two just persons from among you﴾ over the taking back or the separation. ﴿And establish the testimony for Allah﴾ not for the one against whom it is given, nor for him. ﴿That is what is enjoined upon whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ from the distress of this world and the Hereafter.

﴿And He will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ it occurs to his mind. ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah﴾ in his affairs, ﴿then He is sufficient for him﴾ He is enough for him. ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾ His will is carried out. ﴿Allah has already set a decree for everything﴾ such as ease and hardship, ﴿a due measure﴾ an appointed time.

﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation﴾, written with a hamzah and a yā' and without the yā' in both places, meaning the menstruation (ḥayḍ), ﴿from among your women, if you doubt﴾, that is, you are in doubt about their waiting period ('iddah), ﴿then their waiting period is three months. And those who have not menstruated﴾ because of their youth, ﴿then their waiting period is three months.﴾ These two rulings concern women other than widows. As for widows, their waiting period is what is in the verse: ﴿they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾. ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is that they lay down their burden﴾, meaning the end of their waiting period, whether they are divorced or widowed. ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair﴾, in this world and the Hereafter.
That which is mentioned regarding the waiting period (ʿiddah) — "that" — is the command of Allah, His ruling.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 65, verse 6:

﴿Let them dwell﴾ i.e., the divorced women, ﴿where you dwell﴾ i.e., in some of your dwellings, ﴿according to your means﴾ i.e., your capacity. It is an explicative apposition (ʿatf bayan) or a substitute (badal) for what precedes it, with the preposition repeated, and a noun is understood: i.e., the places of your capacity, not what falls short of it. ﴿And do not harm them so as to constrain them﴾ by the dwellings, so that they are forced to go out, or by the maintenance, so that they ransom themselves from you. ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth to their burden. Then if they nurse for you﴾ your children from them, ﴿give them their payment﴾ for the nursing. ﴿And confer among yourselves with kindness﴾ between you and them, ﴿with kindness﴾, i.e., with goodness regarding the children, by agreeing upon a known wage for the nursing. ﴿And if you disagree﴾ i.e., you are at odds regarding the nursing, so that the father refuses the wage and the mother refuses to nurse, ﴿then another woman shall nurse for him﴾ for the father, ﴿another﴾. The mother is not compelled to nurse him.

﴿Let him spend﴾ on the divorced women and the nursing mothers, ﴿the man of means from his means, and he whose provision is restricted﴾, meaning constricted, ﴿let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾, meaning what Allah has bestowed upon him, ﴿according to his capacity. Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it. Allah will bring about ease after hardship﴾, and He has done so through al-futuh (the openings of provision, i.e., conquests and abundance).

The commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 65, verse 8:

﴿And how many a town﴾ — "how many" (kam). The kaf here is the kaf of comparison (kaf al-jarr) entering upon ayyin, meaning "how many." ﴿from a town﴾ — i.e., and many of the towns. ﴿rebelled﴾ — disobeyed, meaning its people, ﴿against the command of its Lord and His messengers. So We called it to account﴾ — in the Hereafter, even though it has not yet come, because its occurrence is certain, ﴿with a severe reckoning, and We punished it with a terrible punishment﴾ — with the kaf pronounced with sukun or with damma (nukr), i.e., dreadful, and it is the punishment of the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 65, verse 9:

﴿So it tasted the consequence of its affair﴾, its punishment, ﴿and the outcome of its affair was loss﴾, loss and destruction.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 65, verse 10:

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment.﴾ The repetition of the threat is for emphasis. ﴿So fear Allah, O you of understanding,﴾ meaning, those possessed of intellect. ﴿Who have believed,﴾ is an attribute of the addressed (al-munada) or an explanation of it. ﴿Allah has sent down to you a reminder,﴾ which is the Qur'an.

﴿A messenger﴾: that is, Muhammad (ﷺ), in the accusative governed by a verb understood, meaning "and He sent." ﴿reciting to you the clear signs of Allah﴾, read with the yāʾ either open or with a kasra, as has been mentioned before, ﴿that He may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ after the coming of the Reminder and the Messenger, ﴿from darknesses﴾, meaning disbelief in which they were, ﴿into light﴾, meaning the faith that has taken hold of them after disbelief. ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will admit him﴾, and in another reading with the nūn, ﴿into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has indeed made good provision for him﴾, that is, the provision of Paradise, whose bounty never ends.

Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them, (i.e., seven earths), [His] command descends between them (i.e., the revelation), and Gabriel brings it down between the heavens and the earth, descending from the seventh heaven to the seventh earth, so that you may know (it is connected to a omitted verb; i.e., He informs you of that creation and descent).
